articles.title: Five UFC contracts awarded after DWCS 10 - Week 3
articles.summary: Following the third week of Dana White's Contender Series 10, five UFC contracts were awarded.
articles.body:
The third week of the 10th season of Dana White's Contender Series took place on Tuesday at the Meta Apex in Las Vegas. The fight card featured five fights with 10 athletes competing for a spot on the UFC roster. Four of the bouts ended in finishes and five athletes received UFC contract offers.

The fight card was headlined by a women's bantamweight but between Bella Mir , the daughter of former multiple time UFC heavyweight champion Frank Mir , and Alex Apodaca. Despite being an astronomical underdog, Apodaca won via unanimous decision and received a UFC contract.

Heavyweight Guilherme Uriel earned an offer from the fight promotion for his 50-second submission win over Mario Piazzon in the co-featured contest.

Welterweight Sean Clancy Jr. secured a place on the UFC roster with his second-round TKO win over Gary Balletto Jr. He put an end to the fight with a series of brutal elbows.

Welterweight Ronald Humphrey was offered a UFC contract after his first-round submission win over Alexis Miranda. He forced a bloodied Miranda to tap out to a rear-naked choke.

Middleweight Nick Galanti only needed 35 seconds to finish Carlos Petruzzella via knockout to kick off the night of fights. After dropping Petruzzella with a right hand, Galanti went in for the kill with a series of unanswered punches.

articles.title: The âIndian Rhinoâ Chungreng Koren finds his way back with a UFC contract within reach
articles.summary: MMA News: Chungreng Koren is lighter now. He is also more prepared.That may sound like a simple observation ahead of his Road to UFC Season 5 bantamweight semif.
articles.body: Chungreng Koren is lighter now. He is also more prepared.That may sound like a simple observation ahead of his Road to UFC Season 5 bantamweight semifinal against Japanâs Ryo Tajima in Shanghai on August 28. For Koren, though, the difference between this camp and the one that preceded his quarterfinal is significant.When he arrived in Macau for the opening round in May, Koren had accepted the fight at short notice after initially being named a backup.He missed weight before facing Japanâs previously unbeaten Ryuho Miyaguchi. Still, inside the cage he delivered one of the more impressive performances of the opening round, dropping Miyaguchi with a left hand before finishing him with a rear-naked choke at 4:00 of the second round.This time, Koren says, the preparation has been different.âIt was very different. In the last bout, I just did sauna and tried to lose weight. I didn't want to miss the opportunity, so I went for it,â Koren told TimesofIndia.com ahead of the semifinal bout.âThis time, I was at home for three months. I rested for 10 days. After that, I went for training.âA different camp, a different KorenThe weight issue is something Koren is not avoiding. It was an unwanted footnote to an otherwise important night. But Koren admits that the bigger problem was what happened after his previous defeat.In August 2025, he lost his Matrix Fight Night bantamweight title to Nepalâs Rabindra Dhant. The defeat came after Koren had already seen an earlier Road to UFC opportunity disappear because of contractual obligations. The combination left him struggling with his mental health and, eventually, his discipline.âLast time, [when] I lost; after that, I got depressed. I was thinking that I was going to go to the UFC, but I lost. I lost my mind,â he said.âI used to eat healthy food. I used to do regular training. [After that] I didn't go out of my house. I used to eat whatever I wanted. Because of this, my mental and physical condition went down.âThe correction, for Koren, had to begin with the basics.âIf we want to fight, we have to be disciplined. But I lost my discipline. That's why I could not lose weight. Now, I want to eat healthy food. I want to maintain my body. I want to recoverâ.The numbers tell part of that change. Koren says he came into the previous fight around 71 kg and is now down to around 66-67 kg.There has been work on his game too. After the Dhant loss, Koren travelled to Dagestan, where he trained with wrestlers, strikers and UFC fighters. He had previously described that period as a reset, saying it helped him move away from relying primarily on toughness and pressure and towards greater attention to technique, timing and discipline.Ahead of Tajima, he has also spent time training in Phuket.âI have recently trained in Phuket. I have very good partners there. UFC fighters trained with me and [we] fought together. So, I am ready to give a good performance this time,â Koren said.The improvement he feels most strongly is in his striking. âI have improved my striking,â he said when asked what had changed most since the Dhant defeat.That improvement was visible against Miyaguchi. The Japanese fighter began finding his range early in the second round, landing straight right hands. Koren responded with the left hand that dropped him, followed the opening with ground strikes and eventually moved to the back for the submission.Ryo Tajima presents a different testTajima, though, offers a different problem. He is 11-3 and comes into the semifinal after beating Chinaâs Ti Haitao by split decision in May. Koren sees the Japanese fighter as a more experienced opponent with physical advantages.âAny fighter at this level has to be good, and he has more experience than me. He has a better reach than me. He would put more pressure on me. That's why I study him.âKoren's answer to that reach is straightforward. âI think my biggest advantage against him will be my takedown. He has a long reach. So, I think my biggest advantage against him will be my takedown.âThat may be one of the clearest indications of how Koren expects the fight to develop. Tajima has already shown he can handle a three-round fight and blend wrestling with striking. Koren, meanwhile, is coming off a performance in which he showed he can hurt an opponent on the feet before taking the fight to the ground.There is little interest, though, in looking beyond August 28. Koren is now one win away from the Road to UFC final. A victory would leave him one fight from the UFC contract he has pursued for years.But ask him about that contract and his answer is immediate.âOnly one thing at this time.âWhich is?âTajima.âThe Rabindra Dhant rematch can waitThe other semifinal has its own significance for Koren. Dhant is on the opposite side of the bracket, facing unbeaten New Zealander Kasib Murdoch.A Koren-Dhant rematch therefore remains possible. The first meeting ended with Dhant taking Koren's MFN title. This time, the stakes would be considerably higher.Koren knows that, but does not want to get ahead of himself.âWe have to win this fight first. Both the fighters are good. Rabindranath Dant is good. Whatever happens, I have to win this fight first.âStill, Koren sees the possibility of a rematch differently this time. Their first fight had generated significant interest around his profile, with Koren saying it drew more than 50,000 views on his account. If they meet again with a UFC contract at stake, he believes the interest would be even greater.âLast time, we fought in MFN. I had 50K-plus views on my account. And we had good hype. And if I fight Dant, it will generate good hype.âFor Koren, that makes a potential rematch more than just an opportunity to settle an old score.âIt's a good opportunity, and we will have good history as well. But we will see.âThe pressure of fighting for IndiaWhile the focus for Koren is Tajima, that is partly tactical. It is also about the pressure Koren now feels. Before the tournament began, he spoke about carrying his mother, wife, child, people and country with him. In Shanghai, that responsibility sounds even heavier.âThis is very special. We are fighting not just for ourselves. Not for our family. I am fighting for my country.ââAt the same time, there are a lot of risks. If I lose, there will be two or three people to say good things about me. But there will be 100 people to troll me.âIt is a different way of describing what is at stake. The UFC contract is the obvious prize. He also sees the opportunity as part of a larger problem in Indian MMA: there are fighters, he believes, but not enough regular opportunities for them to develop professionally.âIf we want to grow even more, we have to invest in MMA, we have to participate in tournaments, and then only we can find good fighters,â he said.âIn India, MFN is number one. Then there are Ronin FC, Aturto and we have five or six more. But we don't do it [tournaments] regularly.âWhat Indian MMA needs nextHis argument is simple: more competition would create more fighters.âIn other countries, they have regular tournaments, So if we can invest in 20-25 tournaments for professional fighters; very soon, in two or three years, we will find good fighters.âKoren has already become part of that search for visibility. His first Road to UFC run ended before it started. His second arrived unexpectedly. He then missed weight, stepped into the cage against an unbeaten opponent and won by submission.Now there is no short-notice excuse, no backup status and no need to wonder whether he belongs in the tournament.And Koren's message to the young fighters watching is the same one he has repeated through the setbacks.âFirst of all, you don't have to give up.âHe pauses, then repeats it.âYou don't have to give up.âBut he also offers a warning that comes from his own experience.âAnd this is a very rigorous game. And you have to think 10 times before taking this step. And if you want to move forward, you have to sacrifice first.ââYou have to dedicate yourself. If you sacrifice first, dedication will come. First, you have to sacrifice. You have to move forward. That's all I have to say.âOn August 28, Koren gets another opportunity to move forward. This time, he has had the camp. He has worked on the striking. He says his body is ready. And, at least for now, there is only one name occupying his mind. Tajima.Watch ROAD TO UFC Season 5 SFs (Koren vs Ryo Tajima) on August 28, 2026, from 2:30 PM IST live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD, Sony Sports Ten 3 SD & HD (Hindi), Sony Sports Ten 4 SD (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada) & Sony LIV.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron: Five years from influencers to queens of women's boxing for upstart promoters
articles.summary: On Saturday, Most Valuable Promotions celebrates its fifth anniversary. One of the feistiest upstarts in modern boxing has given a new platform to the world's best female fighters.
articles.body:
On 29 August 29 one of the feistiest upstarts in modern boxing will celebrate a fifth anniversary.

On the same date in 2021, Most Valuable Promotions' headline bout for its inaugural show in Cleveland, Ohio, featured co-founder and online influencer Jake Paul taking on MMA fighter Tyron Woodley in the boxing ring.

MVP's second event, just under four months later in Tampa, Florida, was a Paul-Woodley rematch.

For a long time, MVP's most notable event featured Paul fighting Mike Tyson.

It came at a time when Tyson was so far over the hill that the hill could not be seen in the rearview mirror.

MVP's reputation developed as it put together cards with names and output that were anathema to boxing purists.

The five-year anniversary card, however, shows a side of MVP which has emerged alongside what some would consider its gaudiness.

And perhaps what takes place this weekend offers a better indication of the promotion's future than the fights that have gone before.

The main card features five women's bouts, headlined by Mikaela Mayer taking on Chantelle Cameron to unify the WBA, WBC and WBO light-middleweight belts.

The primary support showcases Caroline Dubois defending her WBC and WBO lightweight titles against Amelia Moore.

MVP, for years dismissed by critics as a snot-nosed upstart of a promotion, is now a major player and the primary UK promoter of women's boxing.

"Respect is the biggest change. I've seen and felt it," Dubois told BBC Sport.

"I remember if you said you're a female boxer, people would look at you like 'ah' â but now people are like 'OK, let's see you fight' â it's not a joke, a gimmick, a side caricature. It's part of the real deal."

Fellow Briton Cameron left promoter Queensberry for MVP last year.

Her WBC interim title fight against Patricia Berghult in November 2024 was a co-main event at Birmingham's BP Pulse Arena.

Eight months later, Cameron fought Jessica Camara at New York's iconic Madison Square Garden on her MVP debut.

She returns to the BP Pulse on Saturday, this time a headline fight for her biggest bout since a 2023 double-header against Katie Taylor.

"MVP are taking over women's boxing," Cameron told BBC Sport. "They've been amazing. Everything they've said they'll do, they've done.

"They got me my world title shot. They got me my Mayer fight. It's all been so quick â it's just my third fight with them."

Before her spell with Queensberry, Cameron had been on Matchroom's books. She beat Taylor, before the Irish superstar avenged the defeat second time around.

"The Katie Taylor fights will always go down in history," she said. "But it dipped. I lost momentum. Went on the shelf. I couldn't get the names, couldn't get the fights, nobody wanted to fight me. I wanted the fights, but they just weren't happening."

Dubois, Cameron, Mayer and Terri Harper are among the top women's boxing talent signed to MVP.

Serrano, Alycia Baumgardner and former undisputed super-bantamweight champion Ellie Scotney are also on board.

So why is MVP the go-to promoter for such female boxing talent?

Dubois has developed a brash new persona since working with MVP - calling out Harper before her previous bout, while some verbal sparring led to a feisty face-off.

Tacky? Some might think so. But it saw Dubois move from fighting at the tiny Park Community Arena in Sheffield to Miami and London's Olympia.

"They've helped me get to that next level," Dubois says. "I want to be involved in the best, the biggest and the most important fights.

"Jake [Paul] brings the social influencer dynamic. He gave me tips and pointers and how I should build fights.

"We're entertainers. It's always good to get that insight from someone who is technically outside of the sport. He has that fresh mindset. MVP have that on lock."

While Dubois defends her titles on Saturday, Harper, who lost their April bout on points, begins her rebuild earlier on the card against Miranda Reyes.

Harper considered retirement after losing to Sandy Ryan in 2024, but she had no such thoughts after defeat by Dubois.

"It's my last roll of the dice to see how far I can push to become a four-weight world champion," Harper told BBC Sport.

"MVP have delivered the fights and a greater audience."

MVP looks to balance its serious stance on women's boxing with its influencer roots - August plans featured an 'MVP x Tiktok Live' event, starring Serrano.

The arena events and headline acts have to stay if MVP is to maintain momentum in women's sport.

"I remember my first amateur fight in Camden, or walking into the gym when I was nine years old," Dubois says.

"Now I'm fighting there and I'm talking about headlining and talking about fighting on Netflix."

If there is one thing an organisation led by Paul can provide, it is talk and spectacle.

For Cameron and Mayer, MVP has the chance to make a real difference in women's boxing.

"I'm an advocate for three-minute rounds," says Cameron. "We've got a long way to go, but if more women started doing what the men do, we can start saying they give us the opportunity for equality for women's boxing."

Fighters like Cameron and Mayer have memories that go back beyond the dawn of MVP. They know how their sport has struggled, and know the work still needed.

"In order for a sport to develop, they need to compete and women are a step behind because we weren't allowed to even compete in the Olympics until 2012," says Mayer.

"It's not going to happen overnight, but this is what we needed to take women's boxing to the next step."

articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron: Mikaela Mayer feels 'unbeatable' ahead of title unification fight against Chantelle Cameron
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron will headline MVPW-06 at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham; WBO, WBA and WBC super welterweight titles on the line in UK vs USA main event; watch MVPW-06: UK vs USA live on Sky Sports on Saturday August 29
articles.body:
British WBO title holder Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena on Saturday - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

WBA and WBC champion Mayer has no shortage of respect for Cameron - who has won her last four fights since a rematch defeat to Katie Taylor in 2023 - but has backed her own ability to unify the titles in front of what is set to be a hostile Birmingham crowd.

"I feel better than ever," Mayer told Sky Sports . "I just know I just feel unbeatable right now. I feel in a great position and I can't wait to get out to the UK and do my thing.

"[Cameron] is good at what she does. She's an aggressive fighter. She lets her hands go.

"She fights at a fast pace and so do I. So that's going to make for a very exciting fight for the fans.

"But I just don't think it's going to be as close and as much of a war as everyone thinks.

"There's probably a handful of people who think I'm stupid for coming to the UK and going onto Chantelle's turf, but I'm just confident in myself right now.

"I'm fighting better than I've ever fought, smarter than I've ever been. And I just believe in myself.

"I feel like no matter where I go, I'm still going to kick butt. So it could be here. It could be there. I'm taking the win."

Mayer pointed to her "versatility" as a defining factor come Saturday, insisting nothing can prepare Cameron for the new and improved version of the 36-year-old that awaits.

"I'm really hard to train for because I've developed so much these last 10 months of being in the gym," Mayer told Sky Sports .

"I know I haven't fought since last October but the things I'm doing now, it's really impossible for Chantelle to have trained for me at this point.

"I'm going to do everything I can to make it a very obvious win, maybe a stoppage, we'll see, but I know I'm coming out with my hand raised.

"I've worked on making sure that my inside game and when I do press forward that my defence is tighter and I'm the one landing my shots. I'll definitely be using a little bit of everything I've got, but knowing mine and Chantelle's styles there will definitely be moments where it will be a dog fight."

'A win would be one of the best moments of my career'

The 35-year-old Cameron won the WBO super welterweight title - a belt Mayer had vacated just months after beating Mary Spencer for it - with a dominant victory over Michaela Kotaskova in April.

The significance of the chance to become unified world champion by reclaiming the WBO crown is not lost on Mayer, with the American describing the prospect of victory as a career-defining moment.

"[A win would be] definitely up there with one of the best [moments].

"I've had a pretty awesome career. Even though I've gone through some ups and downs, I think that's what makes my career even more special and what makes these big fights that are ahead of me extra special.

"I've had to go through trials and tribulations - I've had to adjust, I've had to make changes in my team and keep continuing to get better - and I've done that.

"Going in there and having a dominating performance against someone like Chantelle Cameron, who is very highly respected - the only person to beat Katie Taylor - that's going to definitely be one of the best moments of my career thus far."

The upcoming bout may not be the last between the two, with Mayer revealing that a rematch clause has been included in the contract of both fighters:

"Well, Chantelle and I do have a rematch clause on both of our ends, which is unique, but if it's the type of fight that everyone expects, then why not do a rematch?

"Why not give it to the world again? I have no problem giving a rematch when it's, when it's justified.

"Do I want to kick her butt so bad that she doesn't even want to activate that rematch clause? Of course. But if she does, we can go again."

Watch MVPW-06 in Birmingham, headlined by Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron and with Caroline Dubois also in action, live on August 29 on Sky Sports. Get Sky Sports or stream boxing with no contract .

articles.title: UFC DWCS -6000 favorite Bella Mir suffers her first MMA loss in 6 years to Alex Apodaca in massive upset
articles.summary: International Sports News: Alex Apodaca just pulled off the kind of result that completely flips a fight card on its head. At DWCS Season 10, Week 3, Apodaca walked into the Met.
articles.body: Alex Apodaca just pulled off the kind of result that completely flips a fight card on its head. At DWCS Season 10, Week 3, Apodaca walked into the Meta APEX as the massive underdog against Bella Mir. UFC's official results had Mir listed as a -6000 favorite, so the expectation was pretty clear before the cage door closed. Three rounds later, Apodaca had all three judges on her side. She won 29-28 across the board and left with something even bigger than the win: a UFC contract.How Alex Apodaca broke down Bella Mir over three roundsThe fight did not turn into an easy night for Apodaca. Mir still managed to land some heavy shots, but Apodaca found ways to make the matchup difficult for her.According to the UFC's official recap, Apodaca kept switching stances and mixed up her striking rather than giving Mir the same look over and over. Her takedown defense was also a major part of the performance. That kept Mir from relying too heavily on her grappling and allowed Apodaca to keep the fight in areas where she was more effective.Nothing was left to a single dramatic moment. The bout went the entire three rounds, with the judges all reaching the same 29-28 score for Apodaca. That consistency made the result even more striking considering the enormous betting gap coming into the contest.Bella Mir leaves with first professional MMA defeatFor Mir, the loss changes an unbeaten record she had carried into the fight. She entered DWCS with a 3-0 professional MMA mark and also had an established name in the sport through her father, former UFC heavyweight champion Frank Mir.After the decision, Mir dropped to 3-1. Apodaca, meanwhile, moved to 8-1 and turned the biggest opportunity of her young career into a place on the UFC roster.Dana White later confirmed contracts for Apodaca along with Nick Galanti, Ronald Humphrey, Sean Clancy Jr., and Guilherme Uriel.Galanti needed only 35 seconds to earn his contract with a knockout. Clancy Jr. finished Gary Balletto in Round 2, while Uriel submitted Mario Piazzon with a standing guillotine.That leaves Apodaca with a very different kind of result. She did not need a finish. She survived three rounds against a heavily favored opponent, got every judge's score, and secured her UFC spot in the process.For now, the biggest number beside her name is simple: 8-1. The biggest result is even simpler. Apodaca beat a -6000 favorite and made DWCS history with one of the promotion's biggest upsets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: UFC: Bella Mir suffers shock defeat on Dana White's Contender Series
articles.summary: Bella Mir misses out on a UFC contract after suffering one of the biggest shocks in MMA history by losing to Alex Apodaca.
articles.body:
Bella Mir has missed out on a UFC contract after suffering one of the biggest shocks in MMA history by losing to Alex Apodaca.

Highly-rated prospect Mir, who is the daughter of former UFC heavyweight champion Frank, went into the contest as an overwhelming favourite but was on the losing end of a unanimous decision.

All three judges on Dana White's Contender Series - a show where winners of fights are often rewarded with UFC contracts - scored the contest 29-28 in American Apodaca's favour.

Mir, 23, has said she wants to win a UFC championship, a Brazilian jiu-jitsu title, a Zuffa Boxing belt and an Olympic wrestling gold medal, but the loss puts a dent in the American's ambitions.

After the fight, UFC president Dana White said the pre-fight betting odds, which had Mir as a massive favourite to win, were misplaced.

"You can't have those kind of underdogs on this show. Anything is possible, and if the Bella Mir fight didn't just prove it - the odds were way out of whack," said White.

"This sport's too crazy to be that big of an underdog."

Apodaca, 32, was rewarded with a UFC contract following victory, while Mir suffered the first defeat of her five-fight professional MMA career.

Elsewhere, Scotland's Sean Clancy Jr won a UFC contract after he stopped American Gary Balletto in the second round following a number of unanswered ground strikes.

The 23-year-old, who is the welterweight champion in UK-based promotion Cage Warriors, extended the unbeaten start to his career to nine.

After the fight, UFC president Dana White said the pre-fight betting odds, which had Mir as a massive favourite to win, were misplaced.

"You can't have those kind of underdogs on this show. Anything is possible, and if the Bella Mir fight didn't just prove it - the odds were way out of whack," said White.

"This sport's too crazy to be that big of an underdog."

Apodaca, 32, was rewarded with a UFC contract following victory, while Mir suffered the first defeat of her five-fight professional MMA career.

Elsewhere, Scotland's Sean Clancy Jr won a UFC contract after he stopped American Gary Balletto in the second round following a number of unanswered ground strikes.

The 23-year-old, who is the welterweight champion in UK-based promotion Cage Warriors, extended the unbeaten start to his career to nine.
